title: Explore refreshing the screen on its own, and when a command writes

notes.author: Jack Roddy/42dfd115
notes.text: Two things to explore, filed 2026-10-09. (1) Refresh over time: event::poll with a timeout instead of a blocking read, then compare the data ref's tip oid to the one drawn and rebuild when it moved; the oid check is one rev-parse, cheap enough every second or two. (2) A write from the CLI tells a running screen: options are the screen watching the ref itself (inotify on .git/refs/foam/data and packed-refs, no messaging needed, but packed refs and worktrees complicate the path), or a socket or pid file the screen leaves in .git for the CLI to poke after a write. Decide after (1) lands, since polling the oid may make (2) unnecessary.
